get.description: Items are in the order the events were written. An item names the object and the identifiers needed to open it; the event's data is not served. Only events about records the person may read now are returned. Keep `next_cursor` and send it back. A read without a cursor starts 30 days back; a cursor is refused with 410 once what follows it is older than that by more than 24 hours, or when it no longer agrees with the log (a restore). One request reads a bounded part of the log: `has_more` says to ask again, even after an empty page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page. Opaque; belongs to this client, person and workspace.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Without a cursor: `oldest` (the default) reads the retained window from its beginning; `now` returns no items and a cursor at the present.

post.summary: Subscribe an https endpoint to the events this credential may read. The signing secret is in this answer and never again. The grant must be renewable (offline_access); one subscription per address, so a second create for the same address is refused with 409 subscription_exists naming the first

patch.summary: Change the address, the events or the description; If-Match (or `version`) guards against a lost update. Changing the address or the events makes the calling grant the one that answers for the subscription

delete.summary: Delete a subscription: its queue is dropped and its secret destroyed

post.summary: Queue the event of an earlier delivery once more; it passes the same checks before it is sent. At most 5 times for one event (409 redelivery_limit_reached), within 30 days of the event (409 redelivery_window_expired), and not while 100 deliveries already wait for the subscription (409 delivery_queue_full: ask again once some have settled)
Stop delivering, including what is already queued (those deliveries end as dropped). Nothing changes if it is already paused

Send one signed webhook.ping now, through the same checks and connection as a delivery. Not retried, apart from the subscription's health; at most one per 10 s and 20 per hour for a subscription, and 4 per 10 s and 80 per hour for a grant, the subscriptions it has deleted included (429 ping_rate_limited with Retry-After; details.reason is interval, hourly or busy — one ping at a time for a workspace)

Make the subscription active under the calling grant. Paused or disabled: delivers again from the present (what happened meanwhile is in the event feed, not sent). Already active: its place and queue are kept; only the answering grant changes, and nothing at all if that is already the caller's

Issue a new signing secret; the one it replaces keeps signing for the overlap. Rotating again inside an overlap replaces only the newest secret and keeps the earlier one and its end; overlap_s 0 ends every earlier secret at once

get.summary: Who this credential is, for whom, where, and what it may ask for

post.summary: What a subscribed endpoint receives: the feed's item, signed
post.description: Standard Webhooks. `X-Synwevo-Subscription` names the subscription, hence the secret. Verify `webhook-signature` (v1,<base64 HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<webhook-id>.<webhook-timestamp>.<body>")>; during a rotation there are two, either may match) over the raw body as received, and reject a `webhook-timestamp` more than a few minutes from now — it is the time of this attempt, not of the event (`occurred_at`). `webhook-id` is the event's id, the same value the feed gives: de-duplicate on it within one grant, and on (subscription, webhook-id) when one endpoint serves several people's grants — each gets its own copy, decided for that person. Answer 2xx within 15 s to accept; 410 to be unsubscribed; anything else, a redirect included, is retried, and later events of the subscription wait behind it: a subscription's deliveries are sent one at a time in the order they were queued. At most 100 wait for one subscription (the rest stay in the log until there is room) and one host is sent at most 300 requests a minute by one worker, whoever subscribed.

2XX.description: Accepted. The response body is never read.

disabled_reason.description: Why delivery stopped: gone (the receiver answered 410), failing (no success for 3 days and 10 attempts in a row), backlog_expired (it fell further behind than the feed keeps events), journal_replay (the database was restored from before a later pause, move, rotation or disable: check the address, rotate the secret, resume), or authorization_revoked:<code> — the grant that answered for it ended; <code> is one of unknown_principal, account_unavailable, workspace_unavailable, not_a_member, credential_revoked, grant_revoked, grant_not_renewable, grant_expired, session_ended, entitlement_revoked. `resume` re-enables any of them under the calling grant.

missed_events_cursor.description: Where pushing last stopped (a pause, a disable), as a `cursor` for GET /events of this same grant: read from it to get what was not pushed, de-duplicating on the event id. Kept after a resume; null if it never stopped or the place is older than the feed keeps.

stalled_since.description: Set while an event cannot be decided because of a fault on the platform's side: nothing after it is sent until it can be, and nothing is passed over.

last_error.description: What ended the last attempt: one of http_status, redirect_not_followed, timeout, tls_failed, connect_failed, destination_unavailable, internal_error, attempts_exhausted; why a pending delivery waits through no fault of the receiver (not counted as an attempt): resolver_busy, destination_busy, signing_key_unavailable, subscription_changed; or why it was dropped unsent: subscription_paused, subscription_deleted, subscription_disabled:<reason>, no_longer_readable, event_out_of_window, event_missing. ServiceUnavailable.description: Service Unavailable: journal_unavailable. A change that takes something back (a pause, another address, another secret, a removal) is recorded durably before it is made; the record could not be written, so nothing was changed. Repeat the call.

scopes.approvals.read: Read approval templates, requests, timelines and eligible approvers
scopes.approvals.write: Start, revise and withdraw approval requests, add comments; manage templates where the person's role allows
scopes.approvals.decide: Decide approvals as the person, hand over their tasks, repair a stalled stage where their role allows
